page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.24xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processors operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz across 96 virtual cores. It pairs this computational capacity with 768 GiB of system memory, delivering a memory density of 8 GiB per virtual core. This configuration provides a memory-optimized footprint combined with elevated clock speeds, serving workloads that require both high per-thread performance and substantial RAM.

Networking performance is rated at a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth, accommodating high-throughput data transfers between clustered instances and backend storage services. The instance provision contains zero bundled local storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Storage persistence must be provided through external cloud storage volumes over the network interface. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly by default. Resource isolation is maintained through dedicated CPU allocation, preventing contention often associated with shared multi-tenant resources.

The primary operational profile of this server caters to large-scale, memory-intensive computational jobs. Systems requiring rapid transactional processing within memory, such as enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching clusters, and large data analytics pipelines, utilize the 768 GiB memory footprint efficiently. Simultaneously, the 3.3 GHz clock frequency addresses computational bottlenecks in electronic design automation, financial modeling simulations, and high-concurrency enterprise resource planning applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.24xlarge is a high-clock-speed, memory-optimized instance designed for enterprise applications that demand substantial processing power and high memory density. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running on the KVM hypervisor, this configuration provides 96 dedicated virtual cores clocked at 3.3 GHz alongside 768 GiB of system memory, maintaining a ratio of 8 GiB per vCPU. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps, facilitating fast data transmission for distributed architectures. The server includes no bundled local storage or integrated graphics accelerators, relying completely on external network-attached block storage for persistence. The combination of elevated clock frequencies, massive volatile memory capacity, and dedicated compute execution makes this instance well matched for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, electronic design automation, enterprise resource planning systems, and complex analytics engines that operate strictly within system memory.
